indian_entity: Indian physician at the Tang court (Narayanasvamin's longevity drug)
chinese_source: Jiu Tang Shu (Tianzhu account) and Zizhi Tongjian, s.a. 648-649
event: Wang Xuance's returning mission brings the Magadhan brahmin Narayanasvamin to Chang'an; under Taizong's patronage he compounds a longevity drug — the emperor dies in 649, and the annalists leave the elixir beside the death
firmness_reason: Annalistic record of a named foreign specialist at court; the elixir episode is told with a moralising edge, so the fact of the commission is firmer than its pharmacology
notes: Dates Indian medicine's prestige at the Tang throne, not any text. Gaozong's reign adds the East Indian monk-physician Lokaditya, sent to gather drugs from the southern seas.
